subject: Workplace Skills
title: Transparency Builds Credibility
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Transparency Builds Credibility.

hook.text: Buffer published all employee salaries publicly. Applications doubled because transparency built extraordinary trust.

buildup.text: Leaders hoard information to maintain control. But information asymmetry breeds suspicion and rumors.

discovery.text: Share context, not just conclusions. Explain why a decision was made and people accept it, even if they disagree.

twist.text: You can't share everything. But sharing your reasoning process is almost as powerful as sharing the information itself.

climax.text: Default to sharing. Ask 'is there a reason this should be private?' instead of 'do I need to share this?'

punchline.text: Share the why, not just the what. Credibility follows.

quiz.question: Why does sharing reasoning matter as much as sharing information?
options: People feel included in the decision-making process
Understanding the 'why' helps people accept decisions even when they disagree
It saves time in future meetings
